subject: CardioNova private connectivity & implementation sprint: kickoff and next steps
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Claire Dupont <claire.dupont@cardionova.com>, Liam O'Rourke <liam.orourke@cardionova.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: CardioNova private connectivity & implementation sprint: kickoff and next steps

Hi Claire / Liam —

Thanks again for choosing Redwood Private. Per our onboarding call, this thread will track the VPC peering / PrivateLink endpoints and the on‑prem package schedule so we have a single place for network artifacts, IP ranges, and cutover tasks.

High level proposal (attached): CardioNova and Redwood agree an implementation sprint focused on three deliverables:
- VPC peering for control-plane telemetry and agent updates (AWS-to-AWS peering)
- AWS PrivateLink (interface endpoint) for inference traffic to avoid public egress
- On‑prem package (air-gapped installer) handoff for their lab cluster

Action items for this week:
1) Claire: confirm the AWS account IDs we'll peer with and a preferred CIDR block range for CardioNova's service VPC (proposal in PDF).
2) Aditya / Karthik: review control-plane ports and suggested security group rules (quick checklist below).
3) Marissa: estimate engineering hours for on‑prem package validation and an expected install window.

Quick checklist (initial assumptions):
- Control-plane (peering): TCP 443 (management API), TCP 5678 (metrics ingestion)
- PrivateLink: interface ENIs in CardioNova subnets; TLS only
- Expected CIDR overlap: avoid 10.0.0.0/16 if possible; our recommended peer range for Redwood service VPC: 10.240.0.0/16
- On‑prem installer will require outbound HTTPS to our artifact repository (or we will provide a staged offline bundle)

Attachments: CardioNova_VPC_CIDR_proposal_v1.pdf, redwood-onprem-install-checklist.xlsx

Please reply with the AWS account IDs and a point of contact for networking on your side (if different from Liam). I'll coordinate a short 30‑minute network sync once we have the account details.

Best,
Monica Patel
Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

From: Claire Dupont <claire.dupont@cardionova.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: CardioNova private connectivity & implementation sprint: kickoff and next steps

Monica — thanks for the recap and the docs.

Account details below:
- Primary AWS account for peering: 123456789012
- VPC CIDR (preferred): 10.1.0.0/16 for our service layer; we can carve 10.1.100.0/24 for Redwood interfaces if that helps.

Networking POC: Liam O'Rourke (included).
We have a change freeze the week of July 5, so we prefer the initial network handshakes this week and plan any aggressive cutovers the week of July 12.

Questions:
- Are there NAT/egress expectations for the on‑prem installer? We can give an IP allowlist.
- For PrivateLink, do you require cross-account VPC endpoints in our management VPC or a peered service VPC?

I'll schedule a 30‑minute call for Friday (Jul 2) with Liam and our NetOps vendor (NetLink) — invite to follow.

Thanks,
Claire
VP of Platform
CardioNova

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Claire Dupont <claire.dupont@cardionova.com>, Liam O'Rourke <liam.orourke@cardionova.com>
Date: Thu, 01 Jul 2027 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: CardioNova private connectivity & implementation sprint: kickoff and next steps

Looping in some technical notes from our infra side — copying the customer so they have visibility.

Notes / clarifications:
- PrivateLink approach: we recommend publishing the Redwood inference service as a VPC Endpoint Service in our service account and creating interface endpoints in CardioNova's management VPC. This avoids cross-account peering for inference traffic and keeps audit boundaries clear.
- If CardioNova prefers peering instead, we can support that but will need to confirm route propagation and ensure no overlapping CIDR.
- Required ports (minimum):
  - 443 TCP (API + model fetch)
  - 8123 TCP (optional, agent diagnostics)
  - 5678 TCP (metrics)
- NAT/egress for on‑prem: installer will attempt outbound TLS to artifacts.redwood.com. If you prefer an air‑gapped flow we can produce a signed bundle with checksums and a documented install sequence.
- Our suggested CIDR mapping: Redwood service VPC: 10.240.0.0/16; cardionova-service: 10.1.0.0/16; carve a 10.1.150.0/24 for ENIs.

Next steps for engineering sync (Fri 2027-07-02 10:00 ET proposed):
- Confirm whether CardioNova wants PrivateLink (preferred) or peering for inference traffic
- Exchange VPC IDs and subnet IDs for endpoint placement
- Confirm whether NetLink will manage peering setup or give us temporary creds.

I'll prepare a short runbook template for the Friday call (network checklist + rollback procedures).

- Aditya
Senior Network Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Claire Dupont <claire.dupont@cardionova.com>, Liam O'Rourke <liam.orourke@cardionova.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 02 Jul 2027 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: CardioNova private connectivity & implementation sprint: kickoff and next steps

Great sync this morning — thanks to everyone who joined (notes below). I'm putting the agreed plan and owner matrix here so we can convert into a mutual action plan in HubSpot.

Meeting highlights (2027-07-02 network sync):
- CardioNova confirmed AWS account 123456789012 and agreed to PrivateLink for inference traffic; peering retained for management/control-plane only.
- CIDR agreement: CardioNova service VPC 10.1.0.0/16; Redwood service VPC 10.240.0.0/16; CardioNova will reserve 10.1.150.0/24 for PrivateLink ENIs.
- On‑prem installer: CardioNova requested an offline bundle. Marissa to deliver staged bundle and test matrix by 2027-07-09.
- Cutover window: target week of 2027-07-12 for a smoke test on non-prod, then prod cutover the following week pending success.

Owner matrix:
- CardioNova (Liam): provide subnet IDs for endpoint placement and confirm SG egress rules.
- NetLink: assist with control-plane peering and validate BGP (if used).
- Aditya (Redwood): produce network runbook and endpoint service name; coordinate PrivateLink acceptance tests.
- Marissa (Redwood): assemble offline on‑prem bundle + validation checklist.
- Monica (Redwood): create mutual action plan + HubSpot milestone and share the Drive folder with final artifacts.

Open items:
1) Claire to confirm NAT IPs to allowlist for artifact fetch if CardioNova chooses staged online install.
2) Marissa to confirm whether the offline bundle will need an HSM-signed license (we anticipate no for lab installs, may differ for prod).

I'll upload the runbook and updated CIDR PDF to the shared Drive folder and post the HubSpot milestone (HS-87654) by end of day Monday.

Thanks — everyone on this thread is in the action loop; if you'd prefer separate operational threads (e.g., NetLink <> Aditya for BGP), let me know and I'll split them.

Best,
Monica Patel
Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference
